1.1 Verify residency with recovery
RES-US-002 | Proposed acceptance specification | Test data are synthetic; tests are not execution results.
Scope: PULSO connects resident reporting with government triage, field work, engineering, records and
planning. Product commitments follow PRODUCT.md. Detailed workflows, lifecycle labels and role
mappings remain proposed for product and LGU approval. Sprint groupings organize this submission; they
do not claim completed development.
User Story
 As a prospective resident, I want to prove service eligibility safely so that I can
register without being stranded by OCR, camera, or disability barriers.
High-Level Requirement
 The system shall support this user outcome through the controls below. Given
valid front/back images for the supported jurisdiction, when verification succeeds, then
extracted fields, uncertainty, data use, and the next step are shown before registration.
Given mismatch, outside jurisdiction, unreadable evidence, unsupported file, provider
timeout, or low confidence, then each outcome has distinct plain-language instructions
and preserves the usable draft. The server remains authoritative for protected data,
saved state and permitted actions. Success must identify the committed result; an
unavailable service or an uncertain response must provide a truthful recovery path.
High-Level Scenario
 An applicant selects a supported identity document, reviews the purpose notice,
and uploads readable images. The applicant checks extracted details before continuing.
When the image is unreadable or the camera is unavailable, the applicant uses file
upload or requests manual review.

1.2 Create one complete resident account

User Story
 As a verified applicant, I want my reviewed details saved consistently so that my
account and jurisdiction are correct on every device.
High-Level Requirement
 The system shall support this user outcome through the controls below.
Required fields and rules are identical in web, mobile, API schema, and persistence,
including normalized barangay, age/DOB policy, phone, email, and password. Given
duplicate email across any identity store, then registration fails safely without creating a
second account. The server remains authoritative for protected data, saved state and
permitted actions. Success must identify the committed result; an unavailable service or
an uncertain response must provide a truthful recovery path.
High-Level Scenario
 An applicant reviews identity and contact details and submits registration. The
server saves one consistent account. If the response or verification email is delayed, the
applicant resumes the existing account rather than creating another registration.

1.3 Verify email with a bounded OTP
RES-US-004 | Proposed acceptance specification | Test data are synthetic; tests are not execution results.
User Story
 As an unverified resident, I want a reliable, expiring code flow so that I can
activate my account securely.
High-Level Requirement
 The system shall support this user outcome through the controls below. OTP is
hashed at rest, single-use, expires at the displayed time, has bounded attempts, and
has a server-enforced resend cooldown. Paste and one-time-code autofill work; errors
preserve the email and entered context. The server remains authoritative for protected
data, saved state and permitted actions. Success must identify the committed result; an
unavailable service or an uncertain response must provide a truthful recovery path.
12
High-Level Scenario
 An unverified resident requests a verification code, pastes it into the verification
form, and submits it before its configured expiry. The server activates the account once.
A delayed or expired code leads to a controlled resend on the same account.

1.4 Establish an active resident session
RES-US-005 | Proposed acceptance specification | Test data are synthetic; tests are not execution results.
User Story
 As a verified resident, I want secure sign-in and session restoration so that only
my active account reaches my data.
High-Level Requirement
 The system shall support this user outcome through the controls below. Valid,
verified, active residents receive a bounded session and land on the intended resident
route. Invalid credentials return one non-enumerating message; unverified users receive
a verification recovery action. The server remains authoritative for protected data, saved
state and permitted actions. Success must identify the committed result; an unavailable
service or an uncertain response must provide a truthful recovery path.
High-Level Scenario
 A resident signs in and returns to the intended report page. The server checks
current account status on protected requests. After logout or suspension, an earlier
session cannot retrieve the same resident data.

1.5 Recover a forgotten password
RES-US-006 | Proposed acceptance specification | Test data are synthetic; tests are not execution results.
User Story
 As a resident who lost access, I want one consistent recovery flow so that I can
regain access without broken links or account disclosure.
High-Level Requirement
 The system shall support this user outcome through the controls below. The
supported flow is identifier to recovery code to code verification to new password to
sign-in confirmation. /login, /reset-password, web, and mobile use the same versioned
payload; no client calls a nonexistent token-verification route. The server remains
authoritative for protected data, saved state and permitted actions. Success must
identify the committed result; an unavailable service or an uncertain response must
provide a truthful recovery path.

High-Level Scenario
 A resident selects password recovery, enters an identifier, verifies a recovery
code, and sets a new password. The resident receives confirmation and signs in again.
Expired codes or mail failure provide recovery without exposing whether another
account exists.

permitted actions. Success must identify the committed result; an unavailable service or
an uncertain response must provide a truthful recovery path.

RES-US-008 | Proposed acceptance specification | Test data are synthetic; tests are not execution results.
User Story
 As a resident, I want to understand optional verification levels so that I can make
an informed choice and correct errors.
High-Level Requirement
 The system shall support this user outcome through the controls below. The UI
explains benefits, data use, retention, limitations, and whether the tier affects report
handling. Declining optional KYC does not remove the basic reporting path unless a
signed policy explicitly requires it. The server remains authoritative for protected data,
saved state and permitted actions. Success must identify the committed result; an
unavailable service or an uncertain response must provide a truthful recovery path.
High-Level Scenario
 A resident reviews the purpose and consequences of an optional verification
upgrade. The resident may decline or submit evidence. An uncertain identity match is
sent for correction or human review rather than silently reducing access to basic
reporting.
